a: with beams being set in the walls
t: In the walls or in the houses?
p: Vaticanus has timbers set "in the houses"; Alexandrinus "in the walls," as in Ezra 5:8.

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("upon the walls")
readings.plain: with beams being set in the walls

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: with beams being set in the buildings

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text here. "Walls" matches the Aramaic of Ezra 5:8 ("beams are being set into them," the walls) and gives clear sense; the two Greek words differ by a few letters (oikois, toichois), so Vaticanus probably has a slip.

p: Vaticanus says "a place" was found; Alexandrinus says "a volume," as Ezra 6:2 has "a scroll."

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("a roll")
readings.plain: a scroll

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: a place

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Tomos (volume) and topos (place) differ by one letter, and the Aramaic of Ezra 6:2 has megillah, "scroll." Vaticanus's "a place in which these things were recorded" can be made to work, but the scroll is the better reading.

p: Alexandrinus names Ezra's father Saraias, as Ezra 7:1 has Seraiah.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: son of Azaraias

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: son of Saraias

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus agrees with the Hebrew (Seraiah) and may be right; Azaraias may come from the next name in Ezra's list, Azariah.

a: son of Amartheus, son of Ozeias, son of Bokkas
p: Alexandrinus has three more names here, close to Ezra 7:3-4.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: τοῦ Ἀμαρθείου τοῦ Ὀζείου τοῦ Βοκκὰ
readings.en: of Amartheus, of Ozeias, of Bokka
readings.plain: son of Amartheus, son of Ozeias, son of Bokkas

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (Αμαριου for Αμαρθειου; Εζιου for Οζειου, followed by του Μαρερωθ του Ζαραιου του Σαουια)
readings.orig: του Αμαριου του Εζιου του Μαρερωθ του Ζαραιου του Σαουια του Βοκκα
readings.en: of Amarias, of Ezias, of Mareroth, of Zaraias, of Saouias, of Bokka
readings.plain: son of Amarias, son of Ezias, son of Mareroth, son of Zaraias, son of Saouias, son of Bokkas

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus's longer line lines up with Ezra 7:3-4 (Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki), so Vaticanus has probably lost three names by an eye-skip.

a: That year was the king's seventh
t: The seventh year or the second?
p: Vaticanus says "this year was the king's second," which contradicts the verse's own date; Alexandrinus says "seventh."

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("this was the king's seventh year")
readings.plain: That year was the king's seventh

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.en: this year the second to the king
readings.plain: That year was the king's second

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Vaticanus's "second" contradicts the date the same verse has just given, "the seventh year of Artaxerxes' reign"; read with it, the verse names two different years. Alexandrinus's "seventh" repeats the date, and the parallel repeats it too: "He came to Jerusalem in the fifth month. It was the king's seventh year" (Ezra 7:8). So the doubled date in the Plain is the parallel's own.

t: Arrival on the first of the fifth month
p: Alexandrinus adds the day of arrival, "on the new moon of the fifth month," as Ezra 7:9 has.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete; the KJV
readings.plain: and they reached Jerusalem

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (after μηνος it adds εν τη νουμηνια του πεμπτου μηνος)
readings.orig: εν τη νουμηνια του πεμπτου μηνος
readings.en: on the new moon of the fifth month
readings.plain: and on the first day of the fifth month they reached Jerusalem

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus agrees with Ezra 7:9 ("on the first day of the fifth month he came to Jerusalem") and may have been brought into line with it; Vaticanus already gives the fifth month earlier in the verse.

p: Vaticanus calls him "Apsarus" in this verse only.

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: Ezra

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: Apsarus

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Everywhere else the book calls him Esras or Esdras, and the verse goes on about the man of 8:3-6, so the Plain takes "Apsarus" as a slip in Vaticanus. That is an inference from the book's own usage; no witness explains the form.

p: Alexandrinus has "to teach"; Vaticanus has no verb, only "all Israel."

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("but taught")
readings.plain: when he taught all Israel

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: for all Israel

why: The Plain follows Alexandrinus's verb, which Ezra 7:10 has ("teaching its rules and rulings in Israel"). Without it the Greek of Vaticanus leaves "all Israel" hanging.

t: The royal treasury or the temple treasury?
p: Alexandrinus has "the sacred treasury."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: the royal treasury

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: the temple treasury

why: The Plain follows Swete's text, which agrees with Ezra 7:20, "the king's treasure house."

a: with a fine or with prison
p: Vaticanus seems to forbid fines and prison ("not by a fine"); Alexandrinus lists them as penalties.

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (μη] η A; αργυριω] αργυρικη A); the KJV
readings.en: or by a money penalty, or prison
readings.plain: with a fine or with prison

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.en: not by a money fine or prison
readings.plain: but not with a fine or with prison

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Ezra 7:26 lists death, rooting out, a fine and prison side by side. The Greek mē ("not") and ē ("or") differ by one letter, and Vaticanus's "not" makes little sense in a list of punishments. Alexandrinus also has the adjective argyrikē, "of money," where Vaticanus has the noun argyriō; the sense is the same.

a: Blessed is the Lord alone, who put these things into my heart, the king's heart
p: Alexandrinus adds "And Ezra the scribe said," and makes it the king's heart only.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: εὐλογητὸς μόνος ὁ κύριος ὁ δοὺς ταῦτα εἰς τὴν καρδίαν μου τοῦ βασιλέως
readings.en: Blessed alone is the Lord who gave these things into my heart, of the king
readings.plain: Blessed is the Lord alone, who put these things into my heart, the king's heart

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (adds και ειπεν Εζρας ο γραμματευς, adds των πατερων μου, lacks μου)
readings.orig: και ειπεν Εζρας ο γραμματευς· ευλογητος μονος ο κυριος των πατερων μου ο δους ταυτα εις την καρδιαν του βασιλεως
readings.en: And Ezra the scribe said, Blessed alone is the Lord of my fathers, who gave these things into the heart of the king
readings.plain: And Ezra the scribe said, "Blessed is the Lord of my ancestors alone, who put these things into the king's heart

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus reads more smoothly and matches Ezra 7:27, which may mean it has been made to fit the Hebrew. See the note.

a: Of the descendants of Phoros, Tarosotomus
p: Alexandrinus has "Phinees, Gerson," like Ezra 8:2.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete (the digital texts of Swete and the lemma of his footnote differ on the first letter of the second name: T, G or R)
readings.en: of the sons of Phoros, Tarosotomos
readings.plain: Of the descendants of Phoros, Tarosotomus

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: Of the descendants of Phinehas, Gerson

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus agrees with the Hebrew (Phinehas, Gershom) and is probably the older reading; Vaticanus has carried the lay family name Phoros up from the next line.

p: Alexandrinus names Attus son of Sechenias after David, as Ezra 8:2-3 has Hattush.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: Of the descendants of David,

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: Of the descendants of David, Attus son of Sechenias.

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Without Hattush, Vaticanus joins David to the next name (see the note on 8:30). Hattush is the name Ezra and 1 Chronicles 3:22 give, and Alexandrinus probably keeps the older text.

p: Alexandrinus gives 300 for the family of Zathoes, as Ezra 8:5 does.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: with him 200 men. Of

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: with him 300 men. Of

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus agrees with the Hebrew.

a: with his sons and brothers, ten
p: Alexandrinus has eighteen, as Ezra 8:18, and adds that they came "by the strong hand of our Lord."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς δέκα
readings.en: and the sons and the brothers, ten
readings.plain: with his sons and brothers, ten

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (before this it adds και ηγαγεν ημιν κατα την κραταιαν χειρα του κυ ημων ανδρας επιστημονας)
readings.plain: with his sons and brothers, eighteen

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. The Hebrew and Alexandrinus agree on eighteen, which is probably the older figure.

a: ashamed to have horsemen and foot soldiers as an escort
p: Vaticanus has no verb for what Ezra was ashamed to do; Alexandrinus has "to ask the king," as Ezra 8:22.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: ἐνετράπην γὰρ ἱππεῖς καὶ πεζοὺς προπομπὴν
readings.en: for I was ashamed (of) horsemen and foot soldiers, an escort
readings.plain: ashamed to have horsemen and foot soldiers as an escort

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (ιππεις και πεζους] αιτησαι τον βασιλεα πεζζους (sic) τε και ιππεις και A); the KJV ("ashamed to ask the king footmen, and horsemen, and conduct")
readings.orig: αιτησαι τον βασιλεα πεζζους (sic) τε και ιππεις και
readings.en: to ask the king for foot soldiers and horsemen and
readings.plain: ashamed to ask the king for foot soldiers and horsemen and an escort

why: The Plain follows Swete's text, supplying only "to have," the least English needs. Alexandrinus's "to ask the king" matches Ezra 8:22 ("I was ashamed to ask the king for a troop and horsemen") and may have been brought into line with it.

a: I weighed out and handed over to them
p: Vaticanus says "he handed over"; Alexandrinus "I handed over," as in Ezra 8:26.

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.en: having weighed I handed over to them
readings.plain: I weighed out and handed over to them

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.en: he handed over to them, having weighed
readings.plain: He weighed out and handed over to them

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Ezra speaks in the first person in the verses before and after (8:55, 8:57), so Vaticanus's "he" is probably a slip. Swete's footnote also shows Alexandrinus without the 100 talents of gold and with twelve bronze vessels.

p: Vaticanus names three Levites; Alexandrinus has "Josabdus son of Jeshua," as Ezra 8:33 has Jozabad son of Jeshua.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: Josabees, Jeshua,

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (Ιωσαβεες] Ιωσαβδος A; Ιησου A); the KJV ("Josabad the son of Jesu")
readings.plain: Josabdus son of Jeshua,

why: The Plain follows Swete's text, which gives three names. Alexandrinus's genitive "of Jeshua" makes Jeshua the father, as in Ezra 8:33, and leaves two Levites; it is probably the older reading, but Vaticanus makes sense as it stands.

t: Bulls and rams lost in Vaticanus
p: Vaticanus has lost the bulls and the word "rams"; the Plain follows Alexandrinus here (see also the lambs).

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("twelve bullocks for all Israel, fourscore and sixteen rams")
readings.orig: ταυρους δωδεκα υπερ παντος Ισλ· κριους ενενηκοντα εξ
readings.en: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams
readings.plain: 12 bulls for all Israel, 96 rams,

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete

why: The Plain departs from Swete's text. Vaticanus has lost several words, so that "ninety-six" stands with no animal named and the bulls are missing. Alexandrinus is complete and agrees with Ezra 8:35 on the 12 bulls and the 96 rams.

p: Vaticanus has 76 lambs, Alexandrinus and Josephus 72, and the Hebrew of Ezra 8:35 has 77.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: 76 lambs

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; the KJV ("threescore and twelve lambs"); Josephus, Antiquities 11.137 ("seventy-two lambs")
readings.plain: 72 lambs

why: The Plain follows Swete's text here. Vaticanus's 76 makes sense and stands nearer the Hebrew's 77; nothing in the verse forces Alexandrinus's number, as the lost words forced its bulls and rams.
b: Josephus lists "twelve bulls" and then "ninety rams, seventy-two lambs, and twelve kids of the goats" (Antiquities 11.137). His seventy-two lambs agree with Alexandrinus, but his ninety rams agree with no text of 1 Esdras or Ezra, so his figures do not settle the reading.

p: Vaticanus says "they have broken" the commands; Alexandrinus "we have broken."

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: They have broken

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: For we have broken

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus matches the Hebrew of Ezra 9:10, "We have abandoned your commands," and the "we" of the rest of the prayer; Vaticanus's "they" may be a slip, but it also makes sense as Ezra speaking of the guilty.

t: Jonas son of Nasibus, or Joanan son of Eliasib?
p: Alexandrinus has the names of Ezra 10:6.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.en: of Jonas the son of Naseibos
readings.plain: Jonas son of Nasibus

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: Joanan son of Eliasib

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus agrees with the Hebrew (Jehohanan son of Eliashib) and is probably right; see the note.

a: , and we have found no way
p: Vaticanus adds three words that Alexandrinus, the KJV and Ezra 10:13 lack.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: , and we have found no way

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote (om και ουχ ευρομεν A); the KJV

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. The verb has no object in the Greek; the Plain supplies "no way," the plainest sense (see the note). The shorter text of Alexandrinus agrees with Ezra 10:13 and may be the older one.

p: Swete's text follows Alexandrinus here; Vaticanus has "daughters."

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote; Swete's text
readings.plain: Of the gatekeepers

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: Of the daughters

why: The Plain follows Swete's text, which here corrects Vaticanus from Alexandrinus. The list is of men, and Ezra 10:24 has gatekeepers.

a: Then Azarias blessed the Most High God, the Almighty
p: Alexandrinus has Ezra bless "the Lord God Most High, Sabaoth, the Almighty," as Nehemiah 8:6 has Ezra.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.orig: καὶ εὐλόγησεν Ἀζαρίας τῷ ὑψίστῳ θεῷ Παντοκράτορι
readings.en: and Azarias blessed the Most High God, the Almighty
readings.plain: Then Azarias blessed the Most High God, the Almighty

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.orig: ηυλογησεν Εζρας τω κω θω τω υψιστω θεω σαβαωθ παντοκρατορι
readings.en: Ezra blessed the Lord God, the Most High God, Sabaoth, the Almighty
readings.plain: Then Ezra blessed the Lord, the Most High God of Armies, the Almighty

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus matches Nehemiah 8:6, which may mean it has been brought into line with the Hebrew; Azarias, one of the men beside Ezra (9:43), is the harder reading.

a: So go and eat rich food, and send shares
p: Alexandrinus adds "and drink sweet drinks," as Nehemiah 8:10 has.

readings.w: Codex Vaticanus (B, 300s AD), as printed by Swete
readings.plain: So go and eat rich food, and send shares

readings.w: Codex Alexandrinus (A, 400s AD), from Swete's footnote
readings.plain: So go and eat rich food, drink sweet drinks, and send shares

why: The Plain follows Swete's text. Alexandrinus matches the Hebrew, and Vaticanus may have lost the clause by an eye-skip from one verb to the next; but the shorter text makes sense.
